how: v1.1 re-run: every high finding on the held-out half, read by hand in its commit. The half had already been read once (on the frozen v1 kernel, 9e580e8; that sealed record is data/v1/), so these are re-run figures, not held-out ones.

items.label: cannot read
items.why: A binary test fixture (an image or PDF the tests read), not test code. It sits under test/, so it is a test path, and its content cannot be read, so it is flagged rather than passed. A reviewer would call this noise.

items.label: false alarm
items.why: Each "set +e" step saves the gate's exit code (code=$?), stamps a receipt and then fails with "exit $code"; each "continue-on-error: true" runs a must-fail negative control whose failure the next step checks. Nothing is ignored. The rule has no pattern for a saved and re-raised exit code.

items.label: false alarm
items.why: A new, monthly reporting workflow that runs the gate on outside code (vercel/ms) and is documented as deliberately not failing the job, because a surviving mutant there is a finding to publish. It weakens no existing check.

items.label: false alarm
items.why: The removed line gated bridge.mjs, which had been deleted two months earlier; the line produced no verdict (the commit message says so). A diff cannot show that a file no longer exists, so the rule flags it and a reviewer reads the reason.
